title: adaptive_duty_permille accepts negative density (fail-open)
description:
File: python/src/lichen/timing/duty_cycle.py
Line: 45-69

Bug: The function accepts negative density values without validation. Negative density falls into the sparse case (density < 3), returning the maximum budget (20 or 50 permille).

Spec 2a.9 states: "A node MUST use the most conservative (lowest) applicable value when the operating class is unknown."

Current behavior contradicts this - negative density (which indicates an error or unknown state) fails OPEN to maximum budget rather than failing CLOSED to minimum budget (dense case).

Impact: If caller passes erroneous negative density, node allocates maximum airtime budget instead of minimum, potentially causing regulatory compliance issues in dense deployments.

Fix: Add validation to reject negative density or treat unknown/invalid density as dense (fail-closed):
  if density < 0:
      raise ValueError("density must be non-negative")
  # or fail-closed: treat negative as dense
close_reason: adaptive_duty_permille (python/src/lichen/timing/duty_cycle.py) now raises ValueError('density must be non-negative') for negative density instead of fail-open into the sparse branch (negative previously returned the MAXIMUM budget 20/50 permille, the opposite of the spec's conservative-bias requirement). Chose the reject option over 'treat negative as dense': a peer count cannot legitimately be negative, so it is a caller bug that should fail loud, matching the max_tx_ms guard from project-LICHEN-worker6-aze0. Docstring Raises added; regression test_negative_density_rejected covers -1/-10/-255 x both regions; all existing tests/vectors use density >= 0 (ccp13.json: 0..255). Verified no production callers outside duty_cycle.py. timing suites: 878 passed. ruff clean; mypy 0 errors in duty_cycle.py. 3x codereview via reviewer model (kimi-k3): correctness no findings (call-site verification done by implementer), security no findings, edge-cases no findings (guard mirrors max_tx_ms pattern).
